assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Anthem Biosciences (consolidated, Rs crore; FY19 standalone column dropped by tools/authoring/ANTHEM.patch.js). Anthem reports two segments (CRDMO, specialty ingredients) and describes CRDMO revenue as commercial molecules, clinical development batches and R&D services; the engine runs one revenue-growth path and the four-line build sits in businessLines, checked against model revenue in tools/authoring/ANTHEM.ctx.js. EBITDA is on Screener's basis (before all other income; the company's own EBITDA includes other income). Anthem is net cash: treasury income is built in ANTHEM.ctx.js as a yield on average net cash plus recurring items and entered in otherIncome (treasuryYield 0). Valued on P/E, the method most brokers that disclose one use.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the four-line build below. FY27 +13.8%: Q1FY27 revenue Rs418 cr (-22.6%) on deliveries deferred to Q2-Q4; ~60% of the year's revenue in the order book after Q1 (CFO, 22-Jul-2026); management says growth will be 'in line with our historical growth' (~20%) but gives no number, and FY26 delivered 15% against 20% first guided. Our FY27 needs Q2-Q4 revenue of ~Rs1,998 cr, +19% on Rs1,684 cr a year earlier. FY28-29 +18.6% / +18.7%: the four FY26 commercialisations (8-9% of FY26 revenue) ramp over 2-3 years, 10 Phase III molecules start converting in 18-24 months, a new big pharma from Q3/Q4FY27, Unit II (~50-65% used) and Unit III (30-35%) have room until Unit IV (ready end-FY28). Street FY27E Rs2,546-2,566 cr (BOBCAPS, PL, 22-Jul-2026), FY28E Rs3,096-3,115 cr; Jefferies FY29E Rs3,486 cr.

base._why: FY26 revenue Rs2,124.3 cr: CRDMO Rs1,772.7 cr + specialty ingredients Rs351.6 cr (AR FY26 note 41). Within CRDMO, commercial molecules 60.8% of revenue (AR p.35; Q4FY26 deck), development & manufacturing batches for clinical molecules 14.5% (Q4FY26 deck; CFO '~15%', 20-May-2026), R&D services 8.1% by difference (CFO '8-9%').

businessLines._why: Commercial (14 molecules) +17% in FY27: the base molecules come off FY26 destocking ('restocking now', CEO, 20-May-2026) and the four FY26 launches grow from launch stocking ('growth vis-a-vis what we have delivered in March-26', CFO, 22-Jul-2026) but Q1 deliveries slipped; +22% a year in FY28-29 as Phase III molecules convert (two ADCs among the late-stage ten) and big-pharma relationships deepen. JM's FY25-28E molecule table implies ~15% a year from the six large molecules plus ~9 points from launches. Development batches +10% / +12% / +12%: 10 Phase III programmes (lumpy; one late-stage client acquired by big pharma in Jul-2026). R&D services +8% / +10% / +10%: biotech funding +~50% YoY in Jan-Apr 2026 but smaller projects (CFO). Specialty ingredients +8% in FY27 (Q1 -11.5% on West Asia supply disruption; semaglutide API awaits CDSCO approval), +15% a year in FY28-29 (semaglutide API, enzymes/probiotics; dedicated Unit IV food & nutra plant only from FY29).

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (before other income): 40.8% (FY23), 35.7% (FY24), 36.4% (FY25), 39.3% (FY26), 36.1% in Q1FY27 on a 23% lower revenue. Gross margin stepped up from ~57-59% (Q1-Q2FY26) to 64.7-66.3% from Q3FY26 after backward integration of the key intermediate that had been bought from China ('that integration is complete', CFO, 20-May-2026); Q1FY27 65.0% (CRDMO 68%, SI 51%, BOBCAPS). Management guides employee cost ~13% and other expenses 9-10% of FY27 sales and calls 38-40% EBITDA margins deliverable. FY27 40.0%: gross margin ~64% (mix: SI and development batches carry less), employee cost ~13.5% (Unit IV hiring), other ~10%. FY28 40.5%: operating leverage. FY29 40.0%: Unit IV's people and overheads arrive before its volumes. Street FY27E: BOBCAPS 38.1%, PL 39.6%; Jefferies ~39% rising to ~42% by FY29.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 capex Rs211 cr (Screener; CWIP Rs264 cr at Mar-26). Guidance: FY27 ~Rs700 cr, 'and then post that will be about Rs500 crores' (CFO, 20-May-2026); Unit IV Phase I Rs1,200 cr split ~50:50 over FY27-28, so FY28 stays elevated (CFO, 22-Jul-2026). FY28 Rs700 cr = Unit IV's second half (~Rs600 cr) plus maintenance; FY29 Rs500 cr as guided. PL: Rs10-12 bn over FY27-28E.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs134 cr = 9.5% of average gross block (Rs1,404 cr, Screener) after Unit III was commissioned; Q1FY27 Rs30 cr (Rs120 cr annualised). The engine depreciates capex from the year it is spent (CWIP held flat), but Unit IV (Rs1,200 cr) only starts depreciating when it is commissioned at end-FY28, so we use 7.0%: ~Rs130 / 179 / 221 cr in FY27-29E, close to a bottom-up path of ~Rs130 cr (FY27), ~Rs150 cr (FY28) and ~Rs230 cr once Unit IV runs (FY29). Street FY27E: BOBCAPS ~Rs140 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Treasury income is built in tools/authoring/ANTHEM.ctx.js on AVERAGE net cash (the engine would apply a yield to the opening balance only) and entered in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (checked in ANTHEM.ctx.js): (1) treasury income at 6.0% on average net cash (engine path: Rs1,386 cr at Mar-26 incl. Rs158 cr of non-current bank deposits); Q1FY27 financial income was Rs23.6 cr on average company net cash of ~Rs1,547 cr (Mar-26 Rs1,374 cr, Jun-26 Rs1,720 cr) = 6.1% annualised, down from ~8.2% on average gross treasury in FY26 (interest Rs79.3 cr + fund gains Rs9.6 cr) as rates fell; (2) export incentives (RoDTEP) Rs5 cr a year (FY25 Rs5.6 cr, FY26 Rs5.0 cr); (3) miscellaneous income and grants Rs3 cr (FY26 Rs3.5 cr). No forex gains forecast (FY26 Rs58.4 cr with a weak rupee; Q1FY27 operating other income only Rs1.3 cr incl. RoDTEP). FY26 other income was Rs155.8 cr (Screener 'normal' Rs153 cr); TTM to Jun-26 Rs156 cr.

otherTreasury._why: Other non-current bank balances (fixed deposits) of Rs158.45 cr at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 7) sit inside Screener's 'Other Assets'. They are treasury, part of the company's Rs1,374 cr net cash; the engine and the Excel take them out of working capital and add them to net cash.

assumptions._interestWhy: Built in ANTHEM.ctx.js: 7.5% on average borrowings (Rs51 cr at Mar-26 falling to ~Rs35 / 25 / 20 cr as term loans amortise) plus ~Rs1 cr of lease interest and other finance costs. FY26 finance cost Rs6.9 cr; Q1FY27 Rs0.9 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 28.2% because NeoAnthem's Rs78.7 cr loss earned no tax credit; Q1FY27 17.0%. CFO: 'about 25% to 25.5% for this full year' as NeoAnthem breaks even (22-Jul-2026); 25.2% (new-regime rate) once Unit III is profitable.
assumptions._payoutWhy: First dividend Rs2.00 a share for FY26 (19% of EPS; ~Rs113 cr). We assume ~18% while Unit IV is built (Rs2.2-3.0 a share).

dcf._betaWhy: Anthem has no net debt, so WACC equals the cost of equity. Beta 1.0 (12.5%): three customers are 57% of revenue, two molecules ~37%, quarters swing 15-25%, and it has 14 months of trading history; a little above the 0.97 we used for Laurus.
dcf._tgWhy: Top of the house 5-6% range: Indian CRDMO is forecast to grow 13.4% a year to 2029 (Frost & Sullivan, AR FY26) and outsourcing keeps rising.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from 18.7% (FY29E) to 8% by FY42E: revenue grew 22% a year in FY20-26 (Rs633 cr to Rs2,124 cr) with one down year (FY23).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 38%, a little below our FY29E 40%: more commercial volume and bigger customers bring price pressure, and scale-up of biologics is lower-margin early.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from 15-29% of sales (FY27-29E) to 8% by FY42E: maintenance (~6% of sales, FY26 depreciation 6.3%) plus growth capex at Anthem's ~1.4-1.5x gross asset turn.
dcf._wcNote: Operating working capital is 28.6% of FY26 sales on Screener's Mar-26 balance sheet (other assets less cash and deposits, less other liabilities). That is low for Anthem (~42% at Mar-25): inventory was Rs125 cr after a record Q4 (Rs340 cr a year earlier) and has been rebuilt for Q2-Q3 deliveries (CFO, 22-Jul-2026). The engine holds 28.6%, which flatters forecast cash by ~Rs250-300 cr at Mar-27; we say so in the report.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Deferred deliveries all land in FY27, the big-pharma additions scale, two or three Phase III molecules (including the ADCs) go commercial by FY29, semaglutide API is approved and the US biosimilar starts; growth runs ~5 points a year faster and the margin reaches ~42%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: A repeat of FY23: one of the two largest molecules loses volume (destocking, a competing supplier or an acquirer's re-sourcing) while a Phase III programme fails; growth slows ~7 points a year and the margin falls back towards FY24-25's 36-37%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Anthem: four of the six brokers that disclose a method use P/E (Jefferies 65x Sep-28E, BOBCAPS 57x Jun-28E, PL 55x FY28E, Nomura 50x Dec-27E); HDFC Securities and JM Financial use EV/EBITDA. 65x = Anthem's median one-year-forward P/E since 1-Oct-2025 (listed 21-Jul-2025; IPO months skipped; every weekly close plus the 30-Sep close, 53 points; forward EPS = our FY27E/FY28E, which carry no exceptional items, so the pre-exceptional and reported medians are the same) of 55.3x x 1.172 (nine pharma peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their medians over the same window, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +17.2%) = 64.8x, nearest half-turn. Bull 68x / bear 62.5x = 75th / 25th percentile (58.1x / 53.5x) x 1.172. No own-move blend, no growth uplift (sensitivities only). Written by ANTHEM.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check: Anthem's median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since 1-Oct-2025 (EV at each weekly close less the last published company net cash, over our next-year EBITDA, Screener basis) of 37.0x x 1.067 (the peers' EV/EBITDA move over the same window, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +6.7%) = 39.5x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EBITDA plus Sep-28E net cash. Bull 42.5x / bear 38x = 75th / 25th percentile x 1.067. Street: HDFC Securities 35x Q3FY28E, JM Financial 40x Sep-27E.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 12.5% (cost of equity = WACC; net cash), terminal growth 6%, plus net cash at Mar-27.

cover.headline: India's most profitable CRDMO, carried by three customers: on Anthem's own forward P/E and the sector's re-rating the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}}, a BUY by a whisker
cover.lead: Anthem Biosciences discovers, develops and manufactures molecules for drug innovators (CRDMO, 83% of FY26 revenue of ₹2,124 cr) and sells its own fermentation ingredients (17%). Fourteen client molecules already on the market bring 61% of revenue; three customers bring 57%. Q1FY27 revenue fell 23% to ₹418 cr because key customers moved deliveries to later quarters, while the gross margin held at 65%. We forecast EPS of ₹12.2 / 14.2 / 16.4 for FY27-29E, at the low end of the street. Four of the six brokers that disclose a method use **P/E**, and so do we: Anthem's median one-year-forward P/E since Oct-2025 (55.3x), lifted 17.2% for the pharma sector's move over the same window, gives **65x Sep-28E EPS of ₹15.3 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY**, just above the 15% line. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹913; DCF ₹334. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The best economics in Indian CRDMO
arguments.p: EBITDA margin ~40% before other income (43% as the company reports it), ROE ~21%, gross margin 65% since it began making a key intermediate in-house in FY26. ₹1,720 cr of net cash (Jun-2026) pays for Unit IV, which roughly doubles chemistry capacity by FY28, without debt or new shares.

100+ discovery programmes, 10 molecules in Phase III (two ADCs) and four client drugs approved in FY26, already 8-9% of revenue. Two big pharmas came on board directly in FY26 and a third is being signed. All four FY26 Phase III additions came from Anthem's own pipeline.

arguments.h: But revenue rests on a few customers and molecules
arguments.p: Top three customers 57% of FY26 revenue, the top two molecules ~37% (Nomura). A Phase III failure and a withdrawn product cut FY23 revenue 14%; Q3FY26 fell 15% and Q1FY27 23% on timing. FY26 growth (15%) missed the 20% first guided, and management now gives no number. We forecast ~14% growth in FY27, below the street's ~20%.

arguments.h: A full price, fair only against its own history
arguments.p: ₹859 is 83.8x trailing and 60.6x our FY28E EPS; the DCF (₹334) needs ~25% growth for 15 years to reach the price. Our target rests on Anthem's short trading history and a sector re-rating; the upside only just clears the BUY line, so the rule turns HOLD above ~₹860.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): how much of the Q1 shortfall the deferred deliveries recover; management called Q1 the softest quarter of the year.
Semaglutide API approval by CDSCO (expected "in a quarter or two" from Jul-2026) and first domestic supplies.
Signing of the third big-pharma contract (revenue expected in the later quarters of FY27) and progress at the late-stage biotech client acquired by a big pharma.
Phase III conversions (two ADCs among the ten) over the next 18-24 months; the US microbial biosimilar starting supply in FY27.
Unit IV Phase I (₹1,200 cr): equipment orders from Jul-2026, commissioning by end-FY28; the promoters' 18-month lock-in ends around Jan-2027.

sections.title: A Bengaluru CRDMO that discovers, develops and makes innovators' molecules, plus a fermentation-ingredients business; 61% of revenue comes from 14 commercial molecules

blocks.p: Anthem is a CRDMO: a contract research, development and manufacturing organisation. Drug innovators (mostly small US and European biotechs, plus 9 large and 20 mid-sized pharma companies) pay it to (1) **discover** and test candidate molecules (R&D services, billed mostly fee-for-service rather than per scientist), (2) **develop** the chemical process and make batches for clinical trials, and (3) **manufacture** the active ingredient or advanced intermediate once a drug is approved. It works in both small molecules (chemistry, the bulk of revenue) and biologics (fermentation, enzymes, biotransformation), and in newer formats: peptides, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), RNA interference and oligonucleotides. Separately, its **specialty ingredients** business makes and sells its own fermentation products (enzymes, the serratiopeptidase protease, vitamin K2, probiotics, nutritional actives), mostly to Indian B2B buyers. It runs three sites in and around Bengaluru with 2,282 employees (1,117 scientists); 85% of FY26 revenue was exported, 54% to Europe and 27% to North America.

blocks.callout: **So what:** Anthem is a manufacturing business with a research front door. The front door (discovery and development work for 100+ biotechs) is what makes it unusual among Indian CDMOs and keeps the funnel full; the money is made when one of those molecules is approved and Anthem becomes its filed supplier. That is also why revenue is concentrated: a few approved molecules owned by a few clients pay most of the bills.

sections.title: Twenty years from a discovery lab to a listed CRDMO; the IPO was a pure sale by insiders and the PE investor, and no new money came in

blocks.p: Ajay Bhardwaj, a chemical engineer who ran marketing and technical services at Biocon, founded Anthem in 2006 with Ganesh Sambasivam (previously Syngene's chief scientific officer) and K Ravindra Chandrappa (operations). It began as a discovery-chemistry shop at Bommasandra, added biology and fermentation, built Unit II at Harohalli (2017-18) for commercial scale and Unit III (NeoAnthem) for peptides and high-potency work (commissioned in FY26). True North invested in 2021. A 12:1 bonus (Nov-2022) and a ₹149 cr buy-back (Dec-2023) preceded the IPO.

blocks.p: Anthem listed on 21-Jul-2025 at ₹570 a share (67x subscribed; +27% on day one). sections.title: Industry: India's CRDMO market is forecast to grow ~13% a year to USD15 bn by 2029, faster than the world's 9%; Anthem is still a small player in it

blocks.p: Frost & Sullivan (in Anthem's AR) puts the global CRDMO market at ~USD 213 bn in 2024, rising to over USD 330 bn by 2029 (9.1% a year), with commercial manufacturing the largest part. India's market was ~USD 8 bn in 2024 (CRO ~USD 2 bn, CDMO ~USD 6 bn) and is forecast to reach USD 15 bn by 2029 (13.4% a year). Anthem's FY26 revenue of ~USD 0.25 bn is ~3% of the Indian market. The drivers are familiar: innovators outsource more, biologics and new modalities need specialist capability, most of the ~6,000 drugs in clinical trials belong to biotechs that own no plants, and China+1 and the US BIOSECURE Act push work towards India. GLP-1 peptides are a separate opportunity: semaglutide's Indian patent expired in Mar-2026 and most Indian launches still use Chinese API.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the tailwinds that drive the next three years (outsourcing and biotech pipelines) reach Anthem directly, which is why we forecast ~18% a year of growth after FY27. The ones that excite the market most (GLP-1, biosimilars, ADCs) are real capabilities but not yet revenue, and we do not pay for them separately.

sections.title: CRDMO: a deep funnel (100+ programmes, 10 in Phase III, 14 commercial) feeding revenue that still rests on three customers and two molecules

blocks.p: CRDMO revenue was ₹1,773 cr in FY26 (+17.7%), 83% of the total. Commercial supply of 14 approved molecules brought ~₹1,292 cr (60.8% of revenue), batches for clinical molecules ~₹308 cr and discovery services ~₹173 cr. The funnel is the strength: Anthem works on 100+ early-stage programmes, has 10 molecules in Phase III (including two ADCs) and saw four client molecules approved in FY26, one for a big pharma and three for emerging biotechs; those four already supplied launch quantities worth 8-9% of FY26 revenue (CFO, 20-May-2026). All four molecules that moved into Phase III in FY26 came up from Anthem's own Phase II work, not from lateral transfers. Customers tend to stay: a biotech that develops a molecule with Anthem usually keeps it there when it is approved, and big pharmas often arrive by buying those biotechs.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** concentration is the price of Anthem's model, and it cuts both ways. If P-1 and P-2 keep growing with their drugs (JM assumes +46% and +86% by FY28), revenue compounds with little effort; if either is re-sourced by an acquirer, loses share in its market or is destocked, a fifth of revenue is at risk, as FY23 showed. The four new commercial molecules and a third big pharma reduce the dependence slowly. Our base case assumes commercial revenue grows +17% in FY27 and +22% a year after; the bear case is built on a top-molecule setback.

sections.title: Specialty ingredients: a steady, lower-margin fermentation business that has barely grown since FY24; semaglutide API is the swing factor

blocks.p: Specialty ingredients are Anthem's own products, made by fermentation and sold in the open market: enzymes (₹124.5 cr in FY25), the serratiopeptidase protease (₹41.7 cr), some APIs (₹43.2 cr), vitamin analogues (₹39.2 cr), probiotics (₹23.6 cr), nutritional actives such as PQQ (₹22.0 cr) and vitamin K2 (₹18.3 cr). Revenue was ₹284 cr in FY22, ₹336 cr in FY24, ₹338 cr in FY25 and ₹352 cr in FY26 (+3.9%); Q1FY27 fell 11.5% to ₹77 cr as the West Asia war disrupted raw materials. Gross margin is ~51% against ~68% in CRDMO (Q1FY27, BOBCAPS). Management admits the business has been starved of capacity: when a CRDMO project needs a shared plant it gets priority, so a dedicated food and nutraceutical plant is part of Unit IV.

blocks.p: **Two new legs.** (1) **Semaglutide API** (the GLP-1 diabetes and obesity drug, whose Indian patent expired in Mar-2026): Anthem has scaled up, sampled "almost all the big players" and awaits approval from India's drug regulator (CDSCO), expected "in a quarter or two" (CEO, 22-Jul-2026); it targets the domestic market first and claims costs that rival Chinese suppliers. (2) A **microbial biosimilar** made for a US customer that wants to move production to India (two 200-litre trains); site approval takes ~1 year and revenue is expected in FY27, booked in CRDMO.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** specialty ingredients diversify Anthem but do not drive the case: ~17% of revenue at a lower margin, growing ~4% a year since FY24. We model +8% in FY27 and +15% a year in FY28-29 on semaglutide API; we have not modelled a large GLP-1 volume, because approval timing, pricing and share in a crowded generic market are all unknown.

sections.title: Capacity: room to grow in Units II and III until Unit IV doubles custom synthesis by FY28-29; capex triples to ~₹700 cr a year

blocks.p: Anthem has 425 KL of custom-synthesis (chemistry) reactors and ~182 KL of fermentation capacity across three units. FY26 added 130 KL at Unit II and commissioned Unit III. Units II and III are far from full (50-65% and 30-35%), so management says capacity is "not a constraint" until Unit IV arrives. Unit IV is the biggest project in Anthem's history: a 30-acre site (as large as Units I-III combined) whose Phase I (₹1,200 cr) adds 365 KL of custom synthesis and 100 KL of fermentation, roughly doubling chemistry capacity, plus a dedicated specialty-ingredients plant. Civil work was nearly done by Jul-2026 and equipment orders were starting; completion is due by end-FY28. Phases II-III could take total capacity to about three times today's after FY28.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: real in technology, integration and regulatory record; weak in scale and customer spread

blocks.p: A moat is a lasting advantage that lets a company earn more than its cost of capital for longer than rivals. Anthem has one, of a particular kind. Its returns (ROE ~20-22%, EBITDA margins near 40% before other income) come from doing complex chemistry and biology cheaply and reliably for clients who cannot easily switch once a molecule is filed. What it lacks is scale (425 KL of reactors against several thousand at Divi's or Laurus) and spread (three customers are 57% of revenue). Indian rivals (Syngene, Sai Life, Divi's, Laurus, Cohance, Aragen) and Chinese CDMOs compete for the same biotech work.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** a genuine but narrow moat. The integration from discovery to commercial supply, the process technology and the clean regulatory record explain the margins and why biotechs keep molecules with Anthem. But switching costs protect a molecule only while its owner stays loyal, and an acquirer can move supply; size limits the commercial volumes Anthem can win. We would pay a premium for the economics, not for durability it has not yet shown at scale.

sections.title: Quality and regulatory record: four USFDA approvals at Unit I, clean audits at Unit II, no warning letter; old Drugs & Cosmetics Act cases are stayed

blocks.p: For a contract manufacturer the regulatory record is the licence to operate. Anthem's Unit I has four USFDA approvals and Unit II has passed two USFDA audits, plus Japan's PMDA, Australia's TGA, Brazil's ANVISA (first audit in 2024) and EU qualified-person certification; we found no warning letter, import alert or recall in the filings. Unit III (NeoAnthem) is new and will need its first inspections as commercial work moves in, and Unit IV after FY28.

sections.title: Lumpy, not seasonal: quarters swing 15-25% with client delivery schedules; Q4 has been the biggest quarter two years running

blocks.p: Anthem ships campaigns, not monthly volumes: a commercial client orders a year's material in a few lots, and a biotech orders the next clinical batch when its trial reads out. Quarters therefore move with delivery dates. Q3FY26 revenue fell 15% (₹423 cr) and Q1FY27 fell 23% (₹418 cr), while Q4FY26 (₹611 cr, +26%) was a record. Management says the same thing every quarter: judge the year, not the quarter, and do not treat a "bumper quarter" as the run-rate (CEO, 22-Jul-2026). The gross margin has been the steadier line: 64.7-66.3% for three quarters since the backward integration.

sections.title: Revenue ×3.4 in six years with one down year; margins of 36-46% before other income; EPS ₹1.7 to ₹10.5

blocks.p: Anthem grew revenue from ₹633 cr in FY20 to ₹2,124 cr in FY26, 22.4% a year. The path was not smooth. FY21 jumped 74% and FY22 another 12% as commercial molecules scaled; FY23 fell 14% when a client's Phase III molecule failed and another client withdrew a commercial product (RHP risk factor 3); FY24-25 rebounded 34% and 30%; FY26 slowed to 15% as customers ran down stocks. The EBITDA margin before other income has stayed high through all of it: 46% at the FY22 peak, 36% in FY24-25 when one key intermediate was bought from China, 39% in FY26 once it was made in-house. Profit grew faster than revenue in FY26 (+31%) because of that margin, ₹156 cr of other income (incl. ₹58 cr of forex gains) and a falling ESOP charge, despite a 28% tax rate.

blocks.p: Anthem's EBITDA margin before other income was 40.8% in FY23, fell to 35.7-36.4% in FY24-25 and recovered to 39.3% in FY26. The swing is mostly gross margin. In FY24-25 one large client product depended on an intermediate Anthem bought (largely from China), pushing material costs up; during FY26 Anthem started making it in-house, and gross margin moved from 57-59% in Q1-Q2FY26 to 64.7-66.3% from Q3FY26 (Q1FY27: 65.0%; CRDMO 68%, specialty ingredients 51%). Employee costs (~13% of sales) and other expenses (~9-10%) are largely fixed, so margins move with revenue in a given quarter (Q1FY27: 36.1% on a 23% revenue fall). Company-reported EBITDA adds all other income (FY26: 43.4%); we use the Screener basis throughout.

Company net cash rose from ₹624 cr at Mar-25 to ₹1,374 cr at Mar-26 and ₹1,720 cr at Jun-26, helped by ₹844 cr of operating cash flow in FY26 as inventory built for FY25 deliveries (₹340 cr) was shipped. blocks.p: In FY21-26 Anthem generated ₹2,172 cr of operating cash flow and spent ₹919 cr on capex (Screener's plant purchases; the AR also shows CWIP of ₹264-345 cr in FY24-26), bought back ₹149 cr of shares (Dec-2023), raised ₹248 cr of equity in FY22 and repaid most of its debt; the rest became a ₹1,374 cr net cash pile by Mar-26. sections.title: Valuation: 65x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the DCF says the price already assumes ~25% growth for 15 years

blocks.p: Of the brokers that disclose a method, four value Anthem on **P/E** (Jefferies 65x Sep-28E, BOBCAPS 57x Jun-28E, PL 55x FY28E, Nomura 50x Dec-27E) and two on **EV/EBITDA** (HDFC Securities 35x Q3FY28E, JM Financial 40x Sep-27E). We follow the majority: **P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E)**, the earnings a buyer will look at one year from now. Anthem has no minorities, no acquisition amortisation and no exceptional items in our forecasts, so reported EPS needs no adjustment. EV/EBITDA and a DCF are cross-checks.

Anthem listed on 21-Jul-2025, so it has 14 months of history, not five years. Following the batch rule (PLAYBOOK §7c), we use its own one-year-forward P/E **since 1-Oct-2025**, skipping the first months after listing, on every weekly close plus the 30-Sep-2026 close (53 points): price ÷ the next full fiscal year's EPS, which is our FY27E (₹12.2) for dates to Mar-2026 and our FY28E (₹14.2) after. These forecasts carry no exceptional items, so the median before exceptional items and on reported EPS is the same. We multiply the median by the nine pharma peers' move over the **same window** (+17.2%) and round to the nearest half-turn. Anthem's own move, growth and returns do not enter the base; they are sensitivities below.

assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the four-line build below. FY27 +13.8%: Q1FY27 revenue Rs418 cr (-22.6%) on deliveries deferred to Q2-Q4; ~60% of the year's revenue in the order book after Q1 (CFO, 22-Jul-2026); management says growth will be 'in line with our historical growth' (~20%) but gives no number, and FY26 delivered 15% against 20% first guided. Our FY27 needs Q2-Q4 revenue of ~Rs1,998 cr, +19% on Rs1,684 cr a year earlier. FY28-29 +18.6% / +18.7%: the four FY26 commercialisations (8-9% of FY26 revenue) ramp over 2-3 years, 10 Phase III molecules start converting in 18-24 months, a new big pharma from Q3/Q4FY27, Unit II (~50-65% used) and Unit III (30-35%) have room until Unit IV (ready end-FY28). Street FY27E Rs2,546-2,566 cr (BOBCAPS, PL, 22-Jul-2026), FY28E Rs3,096-3,115 cr; Jefferies FY29E Rs3,486 cr.

base._why: FY26 revenue Rs2,124.3 cr: CRDMO Rs1,772.7 cr + specialty ingredients Rs351.6 cr (AR FY26 note 41). Within CRDMO, commercial molecules 60.8% of revenue (AR p.35; Q4FY26 deck), development & manufacturing batches for clinical molecules 14.5% (Q4FY26 deck; CFO '~15%', 20-May-2026), R&D services 8.1% by difference (CFO '8-9%').

businessLines._why: Commercial (14 molecules) +17% in FY27: the base molecules come off FY26 destocking ('restocking now', CEO, 20-May-2026) and the four FY26 launches grow from launch stocking ('growth vis-a-vis what we have delivered in March-26', CFO, 22-Jul-2026) but Q1 deliveries slipped; +22% a year in FY28-29 as Phase III molecules convert (two ADCs among the late-stage ten) and big-pharma relationships deepen. JM's FY25-28E molecule table implies ~15% a year from the six large molecules plus ~9 points from launches. Development batches +10% / +12% / +12%: 10 Phase III programmes (lumpy; one late-stage client acquired by big pharma in Jul-2026). R&D services +8% / +10% / +10%: biotech funding +~50% YoY in Jan-Apr 2026 but smaller projects (CFO). Specialty ingredients +8% in FY27 (Q1 -11.5% on West Asia supply disruption; semaglutide API awaits CDSCO approval), +15% a year in FY28-29 (semaglutide API, enzymes/probiotics; dedicated Unit IV food & nutra plant only from FY29).

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (before other income): 40.8% (FY23), 35.7% (FY24), 36.4% (FY25), 39.3% (FY26), 36.1% in Q1FY27 on a 23% lower revenue. Gross margin stepped up from ~57-59% (Q1-Q2FY26) to 64.7-66.3% from Q3FY26 after backward integration of the key intermediate that had been bought from China ('that integration is complete', CFO, 20-May-2026); Q1FY27 65.0% (CRDMO 68%, SI 51%, BOBCAPS). Management guides employee cost ~13% and other expenses 9-10% of FY27 sales and calls 38-40% EBITDA margins deliverable. FY27 40.0%: gross margin ~64% (mix: SI and development batches carry less), employee cost ~13.5% (Unit IV hiring), other ~10%. FY28 40.5%: operating leverage. FY29 40.0%: Unit IV's people and overheads arrive before its volumes. Street FY27E: BOBCAPS 38.1%, PL 39.6%; Jefferies ~39% rising to ~42% by FY29.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 capex Rs211 cr (Screener; CWIP Rs264 cr at Mar-26). Guidance: FY27 ~Rs700 cr, 'and then post that will be about Rs500 crores' (CFO, 20-May-2026); Unit IV Phase I Rs1,200 cr split ~50:50 over FY27-28, so FY28 stays elevated (CFO, 22-Jul-2026). assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs134 cr = 9.5% of average gross block (Rs1,404 cr, Screener) after Unit III was commissioned; Q1FY27 Rs30 cr (Rs120 cr annualised). methods.why: How the street values Anthem: four of the six brokers that disclose a method use P/E (Jefferies 65x Sep-28E, BOBCAPS 57x Jun-28E, PL 55x FY28E, Nomura 50x Dec-27E); HDFC Securities and JM Financial use EV/EBITDA. 65x = Anthem's median one-year-forward P/E since 1-Oct-2025 (listed 21-Jul-2025; IPO months skipped; every weekly close plus the 30-Sep close, 53 points; forward EPS = our FY27E/FY28E, which carry no exceptional items, so the pre-exceptional and reported medians are the same) of 55.3x x 1.172 (nine pharma peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their medians over the same window, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +17.2%) = 64.8x, nearest half-turn. Bull 68x / bear 62.5x = 75th / 25th percentile (58.1x / 53.5x) x 1.172. No own-move blend, no growth uplift (sensitivities only). Written by ANTHEM.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check: Anthem's median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since 1-Oct-2025 (EV at each weekly close less the last published company net cash, over our next-year EBITDA, Screener basis) of 37.0x x 1.067 (the peers' EV/EBITDA move over the same window, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +6.7%) = 39.5x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EBITDA plus Sep-28E net cash. Bull 42.5x / bear 38x = 75th / 25th percentile x 1.067. Street: HDFC Securities 35x Q3FY28E, JM Financial 40x Sep-27E.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 12.5% (cost of equity = WACC; net cash), terminal growth 6%, plus net cash at Mar-27.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: A repeat of FY23: one of the two largest molecules loses volume (destocking, a competing supplier or an acquirer's re-sourcing) while a Phase III programme fails; growth slows ~7 points a year and the margin falls back towards FY24-25's 36-37%.
